context.why: Stories 1 to 3 are accepted: the API reads and writes complete records and a registered type gets its endpoints. This story changes how a caller proves who they are. Today the API accepts Django REST Framework's one-per-person tokens (rest_framework.authtoken) and mounts dj-rest-auth at /api/v1/auth/, whose login endpoint hands a token to anyone who posts an email address and a password, taking no account of two-factor sign-in, and also offers password reset, password change and account editing. All of that goes. A person creates and revokes tokens on their account pages after signing in normally, using the pages django-mvp-accounts 0.2.0 provides on top of django-rest-knox, and the API accepts those tokens and the portal's own session. Pages on other websites may call the API to read, and to write with a token.
spec_sections: Clarifications: how a person gets a token, can a browser session use the API, may a page on another website call the API
Edge Cases (a portal's token feature is restricted to some people; a person's level is removed while their token is in use)
prior_decisions: decisions.md D8 and planning-notes.md 'Tokens through django-mvp-accounts': the four steps are in django-mvp-accounts' README (read it in .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/django_mvp_accounts-0.2.0.dist-info/METADATA, section 'API tokens'): (1) depend on `django-mvp-accounts[api]` in pyproject.toml and run `uv lock` then `uv sync`, which brings django-rest-knox 5; knox is NOT installed yet. (2) add `knox` to INSTALLED_APPS in fairdm/conf/settings/apps.py. (3) include `mvp_accounts.tokens.urls` at `account/tokens/` in fairdm/conf/urls.py, before the include of mvp.urls if there is one. (4) `knox.auth.TokenAuthentication` first in REST_FRAMEWORK['DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES'] in fairdm/api/settings.py, then SessionAuthentication.

Remove dj-rest-auth: the dependency in pyproject.toml and its entry in the deptry ignore list there, `dj_rest_auth` and `rest_framework.authtoken` from INSTALLED_APPS, and the `v1/auth/` include from fairdm/api/urls.py. No data migration: no release carried the old tokens. Check `uv run python manage.py makemigrations --check` for FairDM's own apps stays clean (a report about the third-party app orbit is not ours).

Settings: REST_KNOX = {'TOKEN_LIMIT_PER_USER': 10, 'AUTO_REFRESH': False} and CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = True, with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS left off and CORS_URLS_REGEX still limiting it to /api/. fairdm/conf/settings/api.py imports the API's settings from fairdm/api/settings.py BY NAME and re-exports them in __all__: a new setting such as REST_KNOX reaches Django only if it is added to both lists there. A test must prove the setting is live (T038's token-limit case does).

drf-spectacular does not know knox's authentication class. Its documented answer is a small OpenApiAuthenticationExtension subclass; put it in a new fairdm/api/schema.py and make sure it is imported when the API app loads. The header is `Authorization: Token <token>`. Generating the schema must raise no warning about an unknown authentication class.

Tests: replace the token fixture in tests/test_api/conftest.py with one that makes a knox token (knox.models.AuthToken.objects.create(user=...) returns the instance and the token string). The make_token_client helpers in tests/test_api/test_filters.py, test_permissions.py and test_urls.py import rest_framework.authtoken at module level: change them to use the new fixture or a shared helper in conftest.py, changing nothing else in those tests. TestTokenLogin, TestTokenHeaderAccess and TestTokenLogout in tests/test_api/test_urls.py test the endpoint being removed: delete them, and name them in progress.md. These edits to existing tests are the ones this brief authorises.

T037 (in tests/test_api/test_settings.py): the revoked, expired and unknown cases must be seen to fail first against the installed knox before the settings change makes them pass, since research.md's claim that knox answers 401 for them is unverified. A revoked token is a deleted AuthToken; an expired one has an expiry in the past.

T038 (in tests/test_api/test_urls.py): the pages' route names are in mvp_accounts/tokens/urls.py. Sign in with the Django test client, open the list, create a token through the create page's form (read mvp_accounts/tokens/forms.py and views.py for the field and for how the new token's value reaches the next page), use that value on an API request, and at the limit confirm the create page creates nothing. A visitor is sent to sign in. Do not assert on wording.

T039: walk the URL resolver under the `api` namespace and assert no route name or path contains login, logout, password, registration or `auth/user`, and that posting an email and password to /api/v1/auth/login/ is a 404.

T040 (test_settings.py): build the client with APIClient(enforce_csrf_checks=True), sign in through the session, and show a read of a private record of the person's own works and a write with no CSRF token is refused with 403.

T041 (test_settings.py): send requests with an Origin header and assert Access-Control-Allow-Origin is present on an /api/ response, that a preflight OPTIONS with Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization is allowed, that no response carries Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, and that a non-API page gets no CORS header.

T043 documentation: the page for people using a portal gains getting, using and revoking a token; docs/portal-development/restful-api.md loses its login and logout sections (around lines 60 to 100) and gains the knox and CORS settings and who may hold tokens. Also write an architecture decision record under docs/adr/ (next free number, same format as the one story 1 added) for 'API tokens are created on the account pages, never exchanged for a password', and change the ADR line of D8 in specs/011-restful-api/decisions.md to its path.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a current, a revoked, an expired and an unknown token, when each is sent, then the first acts as its holder and the others are answered 401.

Given the token pages, then they resolve, open for a signed-in person, send a visitor to sign in, a token created through the create page authenticates an API request, and at the limit nothing is created.
Given the API's routes, then none accepts a password, issues a token or changes a password or account.
Given a person signed in by session, then they read their private record through the API and a write with no CSRF token is refused.
Given a request from another origin, then it may read the response, the Authorization header passes a preflight and no response permits credentials.
Given the failing tests from T037 to T041, when the implementation lands, then they pass, the old token mechanism is gone and the rest of the suite still passes.
Given the two documentation pages and the decision record, when read against the branch, then they describe tokens as they now work and no page mentions the login endpoint.
